paragraphs: Epic Games seeks a Machine Learning Engineer, Memory who will design new memory architectures that work across problems, modalities and products and help create and deliver production‑ready, high‑quality learning models and associated algorithms. In this role you will work with researchers on projects across the company that require memory in different modalities to define general solutions that enable models to represent experience, decide what they keep and what they discard, and to efficiently store, retrieve and exploit memory. Being Epic means being part of a team that continually strives to do right by your community and users, and Unreal projects have been leading the pack of real‑time entertainment with a constantly growing team of engineering experts and to push the boundaries of interactive entertainment.

The requirement for Expert is satisfied by my hands‑on work building interactive systems. I have used JavaScript to implement pricing logic that adapts to changing conditions, and I have built agent streaming pipelines that maintain continuous data flow. I collaborated with developers to integrate these components into larger codebases, ensuring reliable operation. The JavaScript pricing module was designed for extensibility, and the agent streaming architecture supports real‑time updates across distributed services. Both implementations were tested under load to verify stability.

The machine learning requirement is met by my extensive experience with scikit‑learn, TensorFlow and Keras to construct and optimise models, and by deploying them through FastAPI within Docker containers for reliable production use. I have applied feature engineering, cross‑validation and hyperparameter tuning to improve both classification and regression tasks, achieving consistent performance across varied datasets. These practices align with the need to create production‑ready, high‑quality learning models and to critically assess their effectiveness for ongoing roadmap decisions. I also incorporated retrieval mechanisms to manage memory of past predictions, supporting long‑horizon behaviour in foundation models.
